metadata.title: Malik Nabers Has Great Matchup in Week 5
metadata.description: New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers (knee) is off the injury report and in line to play against the division-rival Washington Commanders. After missing Wednesday's practice, Nabers practiced Thursday and Friday and is set to play in Week 5. He had a breakout game last week, hauling in six of seven targets for 112 yards and a touchdown in the 36-24 win over the Arizona Cardinals. The star receiver struggled early in the season but found a groove in Week 4 with new starting quarterback Jameis Winston. He faces an ideal matchup against the Commanders, which has allowed the fifth-most fantasy points to wide receivers this season. Though rain and wind could be a factor in Landover on Sunday, fantasy managers should feel comfortable starting Nabers as a solid WR2 in Week 5.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers - Clear for Sunday
metadata.description: Nabers (knee) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game at Washington, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: When Nabers kicked off Week 5 prep with a DNP due to a knee injury, he told Connor Hughes of SNY.tv that he did "as much as I could." Nabers was able to practice in a limited capacity Thursday before head coach John Harbaugh said Friday that the wide receiver will "be ready to play Sunday," per Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News. Now that Nabers has received clearance to do so, he'll continue to act as the top pass catcher for QB Jameis Winston.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers (knee) will play Sunday
metadata.description: Giants coach John Harbaugh said Malik Nabers will be "ready to play" on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Nabers is coming off a big performance last week against the Cardinals. He should remain in fantasy lineups this week.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers - Expected to play Sunday
metadata.description: Head coach John Harbaugh said Friday that Nabers (knee) will "be ready to play Sunday" at Washington, Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News reports.
metadata.analysis: A knee injury didn't allow Nabers to log any official practice reps Wednesday, but he was back in a limited fashion Thursday and also mixed into drills Friday. Harbaugh's comments indicate Nabers is good to go for Week 5 action, even if the wide receiver ends up going down as questionable on the Giants' final practice report of the week Friday.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers - Practicing Friday
metadata.description: Nabers (knee) was on the field for Friday's practice, Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post reports.
metadata.analysis: With Nabers having progressed from a non-participant Wednesday to a limited participant Thursday, his presence and involvement Friday is another positive sign for his status ahead of Sunday's game against the Commanders. The Giants' final injury report will determine whether the wide receiver carries a designation into Week 5, but all signs point to Nabers being available Sunday.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers Will Be "Ready to Play" Sunday
metadata.description: After missing Wednesday's practice and logging limited participation on Thursday, New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers (knee) is trending in the right direction, with head coach John Harbaugh telling reporters on Friday that his Pro Bowl wideout will be ready to play in a Week 5 divisional clash with the Commanders. Nabers suffered a devastating leg injury in Week 4 of the 2025 season, and while he has played in all four contests of 2026, this was the first week since Week 1 that he returned to the injury report with soreness in his surgically repaired knee. Coming off his best performance of the young season, a six-catch, 112-yard outing against the Cardinals in which he caught his first touchdown of the year, Nabers is RotoBaller's WR12 for Week 5.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers (knee) officially limited at practice Thursday
metadata.description: Malik Nabers (knee) was officially a limited participant at practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Nabers was a non-participant at New York's practice on Wednesday due to a knee issue, but it doesn't seem to be a serious issue, as he was able to return and practice in a limited fashion on Thursday. It looks likely that he will play in Week 5, and fantasy managers shouldn't hesitate to start him if he gets full clearance to play against the Commanders on Sunday.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers - Marked as limited Thursday
metadata.description: Nabers (knee) was listed as a limited participant at practice Thursday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Nabers returned to practice Thursday after sitting out Wednesday's session, but he isn't completely out of the woods yet. An upgrade to full participation Friday could help Nabers avoid an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Commanders.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers (knee) returns to practice Thursday
metadata.description: Malik Nabers resumed practicing on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Nabers was back on the field after missing practice on Wednesday. He remains on track to be good to go on Sunday.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers - Back at practice Thursday
metadata.description: Nabers (knee) was seen practicing during Thursday's media viewing period, Art Stapleton of USA Today reports.
metadata.analysis: After sitting out Wednesday's practice due to a knee injury, Nabers has taken a step in the right direction by taking part in at least a portion of Thursday's practice. His participation level will be clarified later Thursday as the Giants prepare for Sunday's game against the Commanders. Nabers had six catches for a season-high 112 yards and a touchdown in the Week 4 win over Arizona.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers Returns to Practice on Thursday
metadata.description: New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers (knee) was seen practicing during the portion open to the media on Thursday, according to Art Stapleton of The North Jersey Bergen Record. Nabers might not be a full participant on the final report, but it is good news that he is practicing at all after he was listed as a non-participant for Wednesday's practice due to soreness in his surgically-repaired knee. The Giants are most likely just being extra cautious with their star wide receiver. Barring a serious setback on Friday, Nabers should be active as the Giants take on the division-rival Washington Commanders on the road on Sunday. The former first-rounder's overall fantasy ceiling took a hit early on this year when starting quarterback Jaxson Dart (knee) was lost for the season, but he is still a must-start each week when he is healthy. In the Week 4 win over the Arizona Cardinals, while working with veteran QB Jameis Winston, Nabers caught six of his seven targets for a season-high 112 yards and his first touchdown of the season. Check back on Nabers' status for Friday's final injury report to get a better idea of his availability this weekend. UPDATE: Nabers was officially limited on Thursday.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers Expresses Visible Frustration with Lack of Targets in Victory
metadata.description: New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers (knee) is dealing with soreness in his surgically repaired right knee and is uncertain if he'll be able to play this week against the Commanders. Nabers said, "We'll see how the next day goes," when asked about his availability after practice on Wednesday. He also discussed his frustrations on the sideline in Sunday's win over the Cardinals. Nabers said, "I felt like I didn't get targeted much after halftime," which is why he was waving his arms at the Giants' sideline and yelling to the coaching staff several times during the game. He did only get three targets in the second half, but it remains to be seen if coach John Harbaugh and his staff will allow Nabers to behave this way or if it will get him any more work. If he does overcome his knee issues and plays this week, he will be a solid WR3, according to RotoBaller's rankings, where he is the No. 26 WR for Week 5.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers (knee) not practicing Wednesday
metadata.description: Malik Nabers is not practicing on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Nabers is dealing with a knee injury. He did leave last Sunday's game before returning. His status will need to be monitored in practice the next couple of days.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers - DNP due to knee injury
metadata.description: Nabers didn't practice Wednesday due to a knee injury, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: After Wednesday's session, Nabers relayed to Connor Hughes of SNY.tv that he did "as much as I could," and now the nature of that discomfort has been revealed. It's a bit concerning that Nabers went down as a DNP with a knee issue to begin Week 5 prep, especially since he's a year removed from tearing his right ACL. He also told Ralph Vacchiano of FoxSports.com that his shoulder is "a little sore," but the team didn't list that as the reason for his absence. In any case, Nabers' status will be watched as the week goes on to get a sense of his odds to suit up Sunday at Washington.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers - Dealing with soreness
metadata.description: Nabers said he took on "as much as I could" at Wednesday's practice, after which he noted he's dealing with soreness, Connor Hughes of SNY.tv reports.
metadata.analysis: Nabers also relayed that he'll "see how the week goes" as it pertains to his odds to play Sunday at Washington. He's already on his second signal-caller of the campaign (Jameis Winston) and has a cumulative 18-208-1 line on 26 targets through four games, and whether or not he'll be available in Week 5 remains to be seen.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers Misses Practice on Wednesday with Knee Issue
metadata.description: New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers (knee) did not practice on Wednesday due to a knee issue, per Connor Hughes of SNY. Hughes reports that Nabers admitted he was "more sore than usual." Nabers has recorded 18 catches for 208 yards and a touchdown on 26 targets across four games so far in 2026. The 23-year-old missed most of the 2025 season after suffering a serious knee injury in Week 4. While it's not yet clear if his current soreness is connected to his previous knee issues, Nabers' health status is obviously worth monitoring for fantasy managers leading into New York's Week 5 matchup against the Washington Commanders. If Nabers is unable to play in Week 5, Giants wideouts Malachi Fields, Darnell Mooney, and Charlie Jones could all be in line for expanded workloads against Washington.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers leads team in receiving Sunday
metadata.description: Malik Nabers caught 6-of-7 targets for 112 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 36-24 win over the Arizona Cardinals.
metadata.analysis: The star wideout seemed to be back to form on Sunday. He finished as the team's top receiver with over 100 yards and a touchdown in their nice win over the Cardinals. It finally looked like he and QB Jameis Winston were on the same page, which bodes well for his future fantasy value moving forward.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers - Gets on same page with Winston in Week 4 win
metadata.description: Nabers caught six of seven targets for 112 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 36-24 win over the Cardinals.
metadata.analysis: It was Nabers' best effort of the season, as he began to build some chemistry with new starting QB Jameis Winston, The duo connected on a 25-yard TD in the second quarter, Nabers' first trip to the end zone in 2026, and his 39-yard grab on the Giants' first possession helped set up a field goal. The third-year wideout will take an 18-208-1 line on 26 targets through four games, and renewed optimism in his big-play upside without Jaxson Dart (knee) under center, into a Week 5 road clash with the Commanders.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers is Impressive in Week 4 Victory
metadata.description: New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers put together his best game of the season during Sunday's contest against the Arizona Cardinals. Nabers appears to be finally building some chemistry with quarterback Jameis Winston. The third-year wideout hauled in six of his seven targets for 112 yards and a touchdown in the win. The touchdown came on a 25-yard pass in the second quarter. The expectation was that Nabers would see his value decrease with Jaxson Dart (knee) done for the year. The 23-year-old might be okay with Winston tossing him deep balls. Nabers will have big-play upside against a shaky Washington Commanders defense in Week 5.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers in Position to Explode Against Depleted Cardinals Secondary
metadata.description: New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers caught five of six targets for 26 yards in the 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans. Amid nasty weather and a run-first Giants offense, Nabers couldn't produce again, as he starts his season slowly. In three games, he has caught 12 of 19 targets for 96 yards, averaging 5.2 half-PPR fantasy points per game, which ranks him as the WR71 on a per-game basis. His struggles with quarterback Jameis Winston are evident, and both are hoping to bounce back against an Arizona Cardinals secondary that has allowed the second-most fantasy points to wide receivers this season. With Cardinals cornerbacks Will Johnson (neck) and Garrett Williams (achilles) ruled out and Max Melton (toe) questionable, Nabers and the Giants' receivers should be able to produce. As he looks to kick-start his slow start, Nabers is a low-end WR2 with WR1 upside in Week 4.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers' Fantasy Stock Keeps Sliding
metadata.description: New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers has been one of the bigger disappointments through three games. After opening the season with six catches for 69 yards against Dallas, he has totaled just six receptions for 27 yards over the last two weeks. The Giants have still looked his way 10 times in that span, so this is not a case of Nabers disappearing from the offense. The problem is what those chances have turned into. Jaxson Dart is out for the rest of the regular season with a knee injury, and Jameis Winston managed only 118 passing yards without a touchdown in last week's win over Tennessee. New York has since added J.J. McCarthy, but Winston remains the starter for now. Nabers is still the clear top receiver here, and his shoulder is no longer on the injury report. Even so, the combination of a cold two-game stretch and an unsettled quarterback situation has pushed his fantasy value down heading into Sunday's matchup with Arizona.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers underwhelming in win Sunday
metadata.description: Malik Nabers hauled in 5-of-6 targets for just 26 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans.
metadata.analysis: Nabers led the team with six targets on Sunday, but he was only able to turn that into five catches for a measly 26 yards over the course of the afternoon. He's a very talented player, but it looks like his fantasy output is going to be sparse for the foreseeable future with QB Jameis Winston currently at the helm for the Giants.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers - Team-high five grabs in Week 3 win
metadata.description: Nabers caught five of six targets for 26 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Titans.
metadata.analysis: The Giants' passing game struggled with Jameis Winston under center instead of Jaxson Dart (knee), and while Nabers led the team in catches and targets, he didn't make much of an impact -- his longest gain went for just 12 yards. That doesn't bode well for the rest of the third-year wideout's campaign with Dart not expected back until 2027, but Nabers and Winston will have plenty of time to develop more chemistry. Nabers will take a 12-96-0 line on 19 targets into a Week 4 home tilt against the Cardinals.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers Held to 26 Yards Against Titans
metadata.description: New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers had a quiet day at the office in Week 3, logging five receptions for just 26 yards and no touchdowns in a 12-7 win against the Tennessee Titans. Nabers sustained a shoulder injury during Week 2's loss to the Los Angeles Rams but returned to practice during the week leading up to Sunday's home battle against the Titans. Running back Cam Skattebo led with 40 receiving yards, rounding out a disappointing day for the Giants' receiving corps against a Titans defense that allowed 467 yards over the first two games of the 2026 season.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers a Risky Option in Harsh Conditions Against Titans
metadata.description: New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers enters Week 3 with plenty of question marks after a poor showing against the Los Angeles Rams. Through two weeks, Nabers has caught just seven of 13 targets for 70 yards, averaging just over five half-PPR fantasy points per game. With starting quarterback Jaxson Dart (knee) out for the season after undergoing knee surgery, Jameis Winston is set to take over as the starter. In Matt Nagy's offense, the Giants could lean more on the running game and limit Winston's passing volume, which would hurt Nabers immensely. Despite a great matchup against the Titans, who have allowed the seventh-most fantasy points to wide receivers this season, heavy rain and wind are expected in East Rutherford on Sunday. With a potentially run-heavy script and Nabers' early-season struggles, he is a risky start for Week 3.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers Off the Injury Report, Good to Go for Week 3
metadata.description: New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers (shoulder) is off the injury report and good to go for his team's Week 3 matchup against the Tennessee Titans, per Dan Salomone of Giants.com. Nabers suffered a shoulder injury during New York's Week 2 loss to the Los Angeles Rams, but he was able to finish the game and now appears to be ready for Week 3. Across his first two games of 2026, Nabers has recorded seven catches for 70 yards on 13 targets. The Giants lost starting quarterback Jaxson Dart (knee) to a season-ending knee injury in Week 2, but the team has a quality backup in veteran signal-caller Jameis Winston, who has supported fantasy production from his receivers in the past. Now that he's officially cleared to play, Nabers profiles as a solid WR2 option for fantasy managers.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers (shoulder) officially a full participant Thursday
metadata.description: Malik Nabers (shoulder) was officially a full participant at practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The star wideout was able to log a full practice session on Thursday after suffering this shoulder injury last week. It shouldn't affect his availability moving forward, but his fantasy value is still expected to be lower than it was before with Jameis Winston set to be New York's starting quarterback in place of the injured Jaxson Dart (knee) moving forward.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers - Logs full practice Thursday
metadata.description: Nabers (shoulder) practiced in full Thursday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Nabers suffered a scare when he exited for a spell during Monday's loss at the Rams, but he was able to tough out his right shoulder issue and cap Week 2 with one catch (on four targets) for one yard. While he relayed to Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post on Thursday that he received "good results" from X-rays on that shoulder, Nabers will be on the receiving end of passes from Jameis Winston instead of Jaxson Dart (knee) for the rest of the regular season.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers - Has positive shoulder update
metadata.description: Nabers said Thursday that he received "good results" on X-rays on his right shoulder, Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post reports.
metadata.analysis: Nabers missed some time during Monday's 28-6 loss at the Rams, a contest in which the Giants lost QB Jaxson Dart (knee) for the rest of the regular season. With Jameis Winston under center for most of the Week 2 matchup, Nabers finished with just one catch (on four targets) for one yard. Nabers officially went down as a limited participant at Wednesday's practice, and restrictions on his workload may continue the rest of the week, but his comments indicate that he'll be able to play through his current health concern.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers (shoulder) seen practicing Thursday
metadata.description: Malik Nabers (shoulder) was seen practicing for the Giants on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Nabers is at practice and was seen participating on Thursday. He recently suffered a shoulder injury, but it looks like he is going to be able to play through it in Week 3, barring any setbacks between now and then. Fantasy managers should keep tabs on his status throughout the week.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers Upgraded to Full Participation in Practice on Thursday
metadata.description: New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers (shoulder) practiced in full on Thursday, per Art Stapleton of NorthJersey.com. Nabers suffered a shoulder injury that briefly sidelined him during New York's Week 2 loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Monday night. However, the star wideout was able to finish the game against Los Angeles and now appears to be on track to play in the Giants' Week 3 matchup against the Tennessee Titans. Across the first two games of 2026, Nabers has recorded seven catches for 70 yards on 13 targets. The Giants lost starting quarterback Jaxson Dart (knee) to a season-ending knee injury in Week 2, which creates some uncertainty for Nabers' fantasy profile. On the bright side, New York has one of the NFL's better backup quarterback options in Jameis Winston, who has supported high-level production from his wide receivers in the past. Heading into Week 3, Nabers remains a must-start wide receiver for fantasy managers.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers Gets Encouraging News on Shoulder
metadata.description: New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers (shoulder) got some encouraging news from the X-ray he underwent after Monday night's loss to the Rams. Nabers told Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News that the results were good, though he declined to say whether this is the same shoulder that has given him trouble before. Nabers said after Monday's game that the shoulder popped out and he put it back in before returning. He finished with one catch for one yard on four targets. The Giants projected Nabers as limited for Wednesday's walkthrough, so he is at least doing some work ahead of Sunday's game against Tennessee. There is still a shoulder issue to monitor here, but the X-ray results are a positive development.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers - Limited at Wednesday's practice
metadata.description: Nabers (shoulder) practiced in a limited capacity Wednesday, Connor Hughes of SNY.tv reports.
metadata.analysis: Nabers exited Monday's 28-6 loss to the Rams in the first quarter due to a right shoulder injury but was able to return to the contest, finishing with one catch (on four targets) for one yard. Granted, Jameis Winston took over for an injured Jaxson Dart after the first series of the contest, and now Nabers will be working with Winston for the foreseeable future with Dart slated for surgery on his injured left knee. Nabers will have two more opportunities to get back to full participation this week before the Giants potentially tag him with a designation for Sunday's game against the Titans.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers (shoulder) officially limited Wednesday
metadata.description: Malik Nabers (shoulder) was officially limited at practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Nabers is nursing a shoulder injury that he suffered in Week 2 and was a limited participant at practice on Wednesday as a result. It looks likely that he will play through it in Week 3, but fantasy managers should still continue to monitor updates about his health throughout the rest of the week.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers - Spotted at practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Nabers (shoulder) was seen participating in Wednesday's practice, Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News reports.
metadata.analysis: Nabers battled through a shoulder injury in Monday's loss to the Rams, and his presence at Wednesday's practice is a good sign for his trajectory heading into Week 3 against the Titans. That said, the Giants held only a walk-through Wednesday, so Nabers' status won't be solidified until later in the week.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers Limited With Shoulder Injury on Wednesday
metadata.description: New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers (shoulder) was officially listed as limited in Wednesday's practice, according to Connor Hughes of SNY. On top of star quarterback Jaxson Dart needing season-ending knee injury, the Giants are dealing with an injury to their top wideout. Nabers injured his right shoulder early in the Monday night loss to the Los Angeles Rams, but he was able to return to the game. The 23-year-old only caught one of his four targets for one yard, though, and he could be up in the air to play in the Week 3 contest against the visiting Tennessee Titans on Sunday. For the rest of the season, even if Nabers stays healthy, his fantasy ceiling has taken a big hit with Dart expected to miss the rest of the year. In the Week 1 win over the Dallas Cowboys, Nabers caught six of nine targets for 69 yards and looked good in his first game back from an ACL tear early in 2025. If Nabers is limited at all this weekend or ruled out entirely, Darnell Mooney and rookie Malachi Fields would take on much bigger roles with QB Jameis Winston leading the offense. We will keep a close eye on Nabers' practice status the rest of the week.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers ends with one catch in loss Monday
metadata.description: Malik Nabers caught 1-of-4 targets for just one yard in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
metadata.analysis: Nabers suffered a shoulder injury partway through Monday night's game and briefly left to be evaluated, but he ended up coming back and finishing out the game. He only ended with one catch for a single yard, however, which burned many fantasy managers who were relying on him. Managers should keep close tabs on his health and the health of Jaxson Dart (knee) throughout this week.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers - Major downturn in Week 2 loss
metadata.description: Nabers brought in one of four targets for one yard in the Giants' 28-6 loss to the Rams on Monday night.
metadata.analysis: Nabers exited late in the first quarter with a shoulder injury but was able to return before halftime. However, the Giants' air attack saw a major downturn once Jaxson Dart was forced from the contest after one series due to a knee injury, and Nabers appears to have suffered some of the collateral damage, in addition to whatever limitations his injury may have imposed. Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports Dart has been diagnosed with a sprained MCL, so it's conceivable the star wideout could face the Titans in a Week 3 home matchup with Jameis Winston once again leading New York's offense. Nabers himself is slated for testing, as he stated following Monday's loss that his shoulder "popped out" and had to be "popped...back in" during the game, and that he'll undergo X-rays to gain more information about the issue, per Dan Duggan of The Athletic.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers (shoulder) returns to Monday Night Football
metadata.description: Malik Nabers (shoulder) has returned to the Giants game against the Rams on Monday.
metadata.analysis: Nabers was initially questionable to return with a shoulder injury that appeared to put him in a lot of pain. However, it seems to be just a stinger, and he's back on the field. It's worth keeping an eye on though, as another hit could put him right back out.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers - Returns to Monday's contest
metadata.description: Nabers (shoulder) returned to Monday's game against the Rams in the second quarter, Connor Hughes of SNY.tv reports.
metadata.analysis: Nabers left Monday's contest at the end of the first quarter in significant pain and was even deemed questionable to return by the Giants, but he was able to shake off the shoulder issue and return to the contest.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers (shoulder) questionable to return to MNF
metadata.description: Malik Nabers (shoulder) is being checked out by the medical staff on the sideline with a possible shoulder injury. He is questionable to return.
metadata.analysis: It didn't look like much on the field, but Nabers appeared to be in a lot of pain in the immediate aftermath. He is questionable to return.

metadata.title: Malik Nabers - Sustains apparent arm injury
metadata.description: Nabers left Monday's game against the Rams with an apparent right arm injury and is questionable to return, Ralph Vacchiano of FoxSports.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Nabers was in significant pain after being injured on the final play of the first quarter, and per the Giants' official X account his return is officially in question.
